title: Parenting the Toddler
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Biblical Model of Growth
subpoints: Jesus grew physically, intellectually, and spiritually (Luke 2:40, 52).
The Bible is the primary source for goals and methods in child rearing.
Parents must possess the Word of God to pass it on (Deuteronomy 6).

outline.title: Defining the Toddler Stage
subpoints: Toddler age defined as one to almost four years old.
Rapid milestones: crawling, walking, babbling, talking.
Increased interaction with the world and insatiable curiosity.

outline.title: Challenges of the Toddler Years
subpoints: Frustration for both child and parent due to communication gaps.
Toddlers test boundaries and access dangerous items.
Daredevilish attitude and boundary testing are universal.

outline.title: Biblical Discipline: Paideia and Nouthesia
subpoints: Training (Paideia) focuses on external structure and behavior.
Admonition (Nouthesia) focuses on setting the mind straight and heart training.
Younger children require more external training; older children require more heart training.

outline.title: The Role of Physical Discipline
subpoints: Spanking is a valid biblical tool for training, not to be discarded.
Current cultural trend moves away from physical discipline.
Physical discipline is one of the major tools God has provided for parents.

summary:
In this session of the 'Faithful Parent' series, Pastor Tito Lyro addresses the specific challenges and opportunities of parenting toddlers, defined here as children from one to almost four years old. Drawing from Luke 2:40 and 52, the sermon emphasizes that the primary goal of child rearing is holistic growth—physical, intellectual, and spiritual—mirroring the development of Jesus Christ. The Bible is presented as the ultimate lens through which all modern parenting methods should be evaluated, with a specific focus on the command in Ephesians 6:4 to bring up children in the training and admonition of the Lord.

The teaching distinguishes between two key components of biblical discipline: 'paideia' (training), which deals with external structure and behavior, and 'nouthesia' (admonition), which addresses the heart and mind. While both are present throughout childhood, the toddler stage is characterized by a higher need for external structure due to rapid developmental milestones and boundary testing. The sermon acknowledges the frustration inherent in this stage, noting that toddlers often struggle to communicate their needs and frequently test limits.

Addressing the cultural shift away from physical discipline, the speaker affirms the biblical validity of spanking as a tool for 'paideia,' citing Proverbs 13:24 and 22:15. The message encourages parents to view this stage not merely as a time of frustration but as a critical period for spiritual and intellectual formation, urging the faith community to support parents in applying these biblical principles with wisdom and grace.
